content.title: About
content.content: Poblano pepper is a medium‑sized, dark‑green chile that turns red when fully ripe. In this product it is seeded and sold raw. The flavor is moderately hot with a mild sweetness and earthy notes. It is widely used in Mexican cuisine for stuffing, roasting, and making sauces.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Poblano is one of the most popular Mexican chiles and is known in the U.S. as "ancho" after drying.
Most of the capsaicin is concentrated in the seeds and membranes, so removing them reduces heat.
Raw poblano is often used in salads and salsas, while roasted poblano is key for dishes like chile relleno.
In the United States it is frequently sold simply as "green chile".
The pepper is a good source of vitamins C and A and contains antioxidants.

items.title: Rich in vitamin C
items.content: Vitamin C supports the immune system and aids collagen synthesis.

items.title: Contains carotenoids
items.content: Carotenoids such as beta‑carotene are converted to vitamin A and are beneficial for vision.

items.title: Low‑calorie food
items.content: Poblano peppers are low in calories, making them a good choice for weight management.

items.title: Antioxidant properties
items.content: Phytonutrients help combat free radicals in the body.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: The fiber content promotes healthy bowel function.

items.title: Pepper allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience an allergic reaction to capsaicin.

items.title: Stomach irritation
items.content: Sensitive people may feel discomfort after consuming hot peppers.

items.title: Skin contact
items.content: Capsaicin can cause burning sensations on skin or mucous membranes.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Raw poblano can be thinly sliced into salads, added to salsa, or used as a topping for tacos. After roasting, it is easy to stuff with cheese, meat, or beans. Seeds are usually removed before cooking to lower the heat level.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the peppers in the refrigerator’s vegetable drawer, placed in a perforated bag. They stay fresh for 5‑7 days. For longer storage, freeze sliced pieces.
